title: Jubilee Vessel of Pepi I
image_changes: None; museum JPEG reproduced unchanged. The Walters Art Museum, CC0.
text_changes: Museum inscription field separated into translation, transcription and alternative rendering; wording preserved, HTML whitespace normalized. Longer description excluded.

passages.text: The Horus, Mery-tawy (Beloved of the Two Lands); King of Upper and Lower Egypt, Mery-re (Beloved of Re); First occasion of the Sed-festival; Given life and dominion forever, given life and dominion forever
passages.remark: Alternative museum rendering of the same inscription: Right column: "First of the Sed Festival" Middle column: "King of Upper and Lower Egypt", Mery-Ra Left column: "Horus name=Mery-tawy"; Horizontally " Given life and happiness forever" (this twice)

note: The museum inscription field renders all three labelled columns and the repeated horizontal blessing. Its second rendering is preserved as an alternative, not counted as another inscription. AncientLens scholarly review: unreviewed. Egypt, Saqqara (Place of Origin); Egypt (Place of Discovery). Ownership history: Dikran Kelekian, Paris and New York, [date and mode of acquisition unknown]; Henry Walters, Baltimore, 1914, by purchase; Walters Art Museum, 1931, by bequest.

title: Funerary Stele of Aurelia Artemis
image_changes: None; museum JPEG reproduced unchanged. The Walters Art Museum, CC0.
text_changes: Museum inscription field separated into translation, transcription and alternative rendering; wording preserved, HTML whitespace normalized. Longer description excluded.

passages.text: Farewell Aurelia Artemis, Pasion’s daughter, incomparably sweetest among all.
passages.source_text: Αὐρηλίαν Ἄρτεμειν θυγατέρα Πασίωνος τὴν γλυκυτάτην ἀσύνκριτον ἐν πᾶσι· εὐψύχι

note: The museum supplies the Greek epitaph and its corresponding English rendering; the photograph shows the four-line epitaph below the figure. Egyptian geography, Greek language; no separate Mediterranean count. AncientLens scholarly review: unreviewed. Egypt, Akhmim (Place of Discovery). Ownership history: Dikran Kelekian, New York and Paris, by purchase; Henry Walters, Baltimore, 1923, by purchase; Walters Art Museum, 1931, by bequest.
